title: Two Exceptions
subtitle: Bishop with the wrong pawn, knight against pawns

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter II, §14 The Relative Value of Knight and Bishop, Examples 30–31

steps.title: The wrong bishop
steps.source: It is the greatest weakness of the Bishop, that when the Rook's Pawn Queens on a square of opposite colour and the opposing King is in front of the Pawn, the Bishop is absolutely worthless.

narration.say: White is a bishop and a pawn ahead, and cannot win.
The pawn queens on h8, a dark square. The bishop moves on light squares.
All Black has to do is keep his king near the corner.
Here White wins, with or without the move. The most difficult line:
King to h2. Knight to g4, check. King back to h1.
King to f1, g5. King to f2, h2.
Knight to e3, g4. Knight to f1, and g3 check.

feedback.*: The knight can take with mate.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.
exercise.wrong: The knight can take with mate.
exercise.success: Checkmate. The black pawn on h2 blocks his own king.
